_about: Per-tab CCL manifests (voice_guide_redesign.md sections 3, 8, 9). Each tab declares its supported verbs (caps) and its knob dimensions with a DOM binding + spoken aliases. Consumed by BOTH the shell (explorer.html builds the active tab's ctx from this) and the coverage audit (every live interactive control on a tab must be a bound knob or an explicit exclusion -- unbound control => loud pre-push failure, section 9). Adding a T1 tab is ONE entry here plus a knowledge default file -- never a new tool, prompt, or session-schema change. Knob `values[].v` are the real DOM option values (NOT their display labels); `aka` are the spoken forms a user would say. A knob carries `aka` too, because the word PRINTED on a control is not always its id -- metabolism's `metric` select is labelled Amplitude on screen, so `label` must mirror the live UI text and `aka` must cover what a user would actually say. Knob names and aliases MUST be single tokens: the parser takes `set <knob> <value...>` and reads the knob as the first word, so a two-word alias is unparseable, not merely unmatched. Keys beginning with _ are documentation and ignored by consumers. GESTURES: each tab must also declare its non-DOM interaction surface (zoom, pan, drag, click, hover) -- the runtime sweep enumerates ELEMENTS and is structurally blind to gestures, so they are declared and the gate checks the declaration is honest: `covered` must name verbs the tab actually has in caps, `deferred` must name its increment, `excluded` must give a reason, and a tab declaring nothing FAILS (silence is not a completeness claim).

sociogram._knobs_note: Sociogram's affordances are filters/selection/highlight/camera (their own dim kinds, not `set` knobs). It carries no `set` verb in v1. Listed here so the shell can read one uniform per-tab source; its caps mirror the engine's SOCIOGRAM_CAPS until step 2 migrates the shell to read caps from this file.

dim_coverage.note: the 32 group checkboxes -- show/hide/only, batch-written through groupVisibility
section toggles; CCL reaches these as section terms ('only traditions')
find / clear (Clear's onclick also calls runSearch)

controls_excluded.reason: continuous fields; excluded from the semantic tier by design (redesign section 14.4) -- not journaled, not fingerprinted
help popovers and the settings gear: chrome, no view state
settings dialog -- API keys, TTS voice and model choice; outside the view-state surface and never spoken by a guest
same settings dialog, reached directly (they carry ids)
the voice control surface's own chrome -- a session cannot be started or muted by voice
metered broker path; CCL find pins it OFF so it can never spend, and the separate `ask` verb owns it (v1-deferred)
opens/closes a separate window -- navigation chrome, not view state

controls_deferred.planned: increment 5 -- promote to declared knobs, same shape as metabolism

controls_deferred.reason: bool toggles (Hold forces, Show hover names), knob-shaped, same v1 gap as above
the left article panel closes only by mouse; `close` covers the right node panel only
external-search toggle changes what find does; unmodelled in the highlight dim

sociogram._coverage_note: Authored 2026-07-25 from the LIVE runtime sweep (window.CCLAudit), not from reading the HTML -- 84 interactive controls, of which the static file shows only a fraction (the 32 group checkboxes are innerHTML written at boot). THREE categories on purpose: dim_coverage = reachable today; controls_excluded = outside the voice surface with a reason; controls_deferred = IN scope and NOT yet reachable -- a real north-star gap, reported loudly by the audit and asserted exactly by scripts/test_voice_shell.cjs so new controls cannot quietly join the list. Deferred is not a synonym for excluded; collapsing the two is how this gate would rot.

gestures.label: Zoom (wheel / pinch / trackpad)
gestures.note: `zoom in`/`zoom out` step the graph's own zoomBehavior; `fit` is zoom-to-everything.

gestures.label: Pan (drag the background)
gestures.note: `pan left|right|up|down` steps the camera a quarter-viewport; auto-framing centres every reveal, so panning is for deliberate exploration rather than repair.

gestures.label: Click an edge (open both endpoints)
gestures.note: Edges have no addressable id in the current artifact, so voice cannot name one.

gestures.label: Drag a node
gestures.reason: nudges the force layout, which re-settles; a transient position is not view state (same tier rule as zoom/brightness in section 14.4)

gestures.label: Hover a node or edge
gestures.reason: transient tooltip; leaves no state to read back, so there is nothing for write-returns-the-read to report

items._note: Items come from the force graph's bound data; selecting one opens its article in the right panel.

metabolism._caps_note: reset/restore are deferred to step 2b: they need a per-tab boot-captured snapshot of all knob dims (redesign section 7), whereas the v1 shell only captures Sociogram bootFilters. Until 2b they report unsupported_here on metabolism (honest, never faked). undo/redo work now via the absolute-vector journal (tab-agnostic).
metabolism._controls_note: The 4 knobs above are the tab's ENTIRE interactive surface, confirmed 2026-07-25 by the live runtime sweep (window.CCLAudit: total 4, covered 4, uncovered 0) -- this replaces the earlier static read of metabolism_view.html, which was the static-HTML gate redesign section 14.8 forbids.

gestures.label: Hover a run marker
gestures.reason: transient tooltip over the raster; no persistent state

items._note: A chart has no addressable items yet; the cursor verbs are correctly absent from its caps.

start_here._caps_note: A content tab: no graph, so no filters/cut/camera. What it CAN do is be walked and read, which is the whole point of the item model.

items._note: Three numbered sections (Orient / Decode the names / See it work). The who's-who entries inside section 2 are a candidate second roster later.

controls_excluded.reason: the page's own links and buttons are navigation into other tabs, which voice reaches by name via `go`

gestures.label: Scroll the page
gestures.note: Walking the sections scrolls them into view, which is the voice equivalent of scrolling.
